people.name: Tiberius Claudius Candidus
people.summary: Severan general who won at Nicaea (194) and probably Cyzicus; his career inscription from Tarraco records commands against Niger, Albinus and the Parthians.

people.name: Publius Cornelius Anullinus
people.summary: Spanish senator and friend of Severus who commanded at Issus (194) and later held a second consulship and the urban prefecture.

people.name: Asellius Aemilianus
people.summary: Proconsul of Asia and Niger's commander, defeated and killed at Cyzicus in 193.

sources.w: History of the Empire after Marcus

people.name: Marius Maximus

roles.t: Commander of Moesian troops at Byzantium

people.summary: Severan general and senator who wrote lost biographies of emperors from Nerva to Elagabalus in the manner of Suetonius, a major (and gossipy) source of the Historia Augusta.

people.name: Julius Laetus
people.summary: Severan commander whose late cavalry charge decided Lugdunum and who defended Nisibis in 197; executed by Severus, jealous of his popularity with the troops.

people.name: Abdsamiya of Hatra
people.summary: King of Hatra attested in Aramaic inscriptions, who supported Niger and resisted Severus' sieges of 198 and 199.

people.name: Sanatruq II
people.summary: Last securely attested king of Hatra, son of Abdsamiya, under whom the city allied with Rome before falling to the Sasanians in 240/241.

people.name: Bulla Felix
people.summary: Italian bandit chief with 600 men who eluded capture for two years under Severus; betrayed and thrown to the beasts.

people.name: Gannys
people.summary: Eunuch tutor in Julia Maesa's household who organised the coup of 218 and commanded at the battle near Antioch; killed by Elagabalus himself soon after.

people.name: Capelianus
people.summary: Governor of Numidia loyal to Maximinus who crushed the Gordians at Carthage in 238 with Legio III Augusta.

sources.w: History of the Empire after Marcus

people.name: Rutilius Pudens Crispinus

roles.t: One of the vigintiviri; defender of Aquileia

people.summary: Consular senator who, with Tullius Menophilus, organised the defence of Aquileia against Maximinus in 238.

sources.w: History of the Empire after Marcus

people.name: Tullius Menophilus
people.summary: Senator who held Aquileia against Maximinus and then governed Moesia Inferior, dealing with the Goths and Carpi after the sack of Histria; executed around 241.

sources.w: History of the Empire after Marcus

people.name: Lucius Priscus
people.summary: Governor of Thrace besieged in Philippopolis by Cniva, who proclaimed himself emperor in alliance with the Goths; declared a public enemy, he vanished after the city fell.

people.name: Mariades
people.summary: Antiochene councillor expelled for embezzlement who defected to Shapur I and guided the Persians to the sack of Antioch; later executed by Shapur. The HA's usurper 'Cyriades' is a distortion.

people.name: Successianus
people.summary: Former defender of Pityus against the Boranoi, praetorian prefect of Valerian, captured with him at Edessa in 260.

people.name: Simplicinius Genialis
people.summary: Equestrian acting governor of Raetia who defeated the Semnones/Juthungi near Augsburg on 24-25 April 260 and recorded it on a victory altar dated by Postumus' consulship.

people.name: Naulobatus
people.summary: Herulian chief who surrendered to Gallienus at the Nestus and received consular insignia.

people.name: Felicissimus

roles.t: Rationalis (finance officer) of the Rome mint

people.summary: Mint official who led the moneyers' revolt in Rome in 271 after being implicated in debasement fraud.

people.name: Cannabaudes
people.summary: Gothic leader killed with 5,000 men by Aurelian north of the Danube, known only from the Historia Augusta.

people.name: Terentius Marcianus
people.summary: Governor who besieged Lydius' Isaurian bandits in Cremna under Probus, attested on an inscription from the site.

people.name: Lydius
people.summary: Isaurian brigand who seized Cremna in Pisidia and held it against a Roman siege until killed by a deserting artillerist.
people.death: killed by a catapult bolt during the siege, 278

people.name: Arrius Aper
people.summary: Numerian's father-in-law and praetorian prefect, accused of his murder and killed by Diocletian before the army.

people.name: Asclepiodotus
people.summary: Praetorian prefect of Constantius I who landed in Britain under cover of fog and defeated Allectus in 296.

people.name: Aurelius Achilleus

roles.t: Corrector in Egypt during the revolt

people.summary: Leading figure in the Egyptian revolt of 297-298, named in papyri as corrector under Domitius Domitianus and treated by Latin sources as the usurper; executed after the fall of Alexandria.

people.name: Sicorius Probus
people.summary: Diocletian's envoy who negotiated the Peace of Nisibis with Narseh at the river Asprudis in Media.

people.name: Crocus
people.summary: Alamannic king commanding a contingent in Constantius' army at York who, according to the Epitome, led the acclamation of Constantine in 306.

people.name: Ruricius Pompeianus
people.summary: Maxentius' commander in northern Italy, killed in battle near Verona in 312.

people.name: Abantus
people.summary: Commander of Licinius' fleet defeated by Crispus in the Hellespont in 324.

people.name: Jacob of Nisibis
people.summary: Bishop of Nisibis, reputed participant at Nicaea and teacher of Ephrem, credited by hagiography with saving the city in Shapur's siege of 338.

people.name: Lucillianus
people.summary: Officer who held Nisibis against Shapur's flood siege of 350; later father-in-law of Jovian, killed by mutinous troops at Rheims in 364.

people.name: Severus
people.summary: Julian's cavalry commander at Strasbourg, who led the Roman left wing and detected the Alamannic ambush.

people.name: Serapio
people.summary: Nephew of Chnodomar who commanded the Alamannic right at Strasbourg; his father, a hostage in Gaul, had renamed him after Serapis.

people.name: Grumbates
people.summary: Chionite king allied to Shapur II at Amida (359), whose son was killed before the walls, leading to a ritual mourning and the furious assault on the city.

people.name: Aelianus
people.summary: Officer who as a protector had led a famous sally at Singara (348) and commanded at Amida; crucified by the Persians after its fall.

people.name: The Surena (363)
people.summary: Head of the great Suren family, second in rank to the king, who commanded Persian forces against Julian's army before Ctesiphon and negotiated with Jovian.

people.name: Sebastianus
people.summary: Veteran general who fought at Solicinium and under Julian, won a skirmish against Gothic raiders in 378 and urged Valens to fight at once; killed at Adrianople.

people.name: Trajanus
people.summary: Officer who assassinated King Pap of Armenia at a banquet (374/375) on Valens' orders and was killed at Adrianople.

people.name: Victor
people.summary: Sarmatian-born Nicene general who served from Julian's campaign to Adrianople, from which he escaped; consul 369.

people.name: Richomeres
people.summary: Frankish officer who led Gratian's reinforcements at Ad Salices, volunteered as a hostage during negotiations at Adrianople, and became a magister militum under Theodosius; uncle of Arbogast.

people.name: Lupicinus
people.summary: Commander in Thrace whose extortion of the Goths and attempted seizure of their leaders at Marcianople triggered the war of 376-382.

people.name: Alatheus
people.summary: Co-leader with Saphrax of the Greuthungi, guardians of the boy king Videric, whose cavalry decided Adrianople.

people.name: Saphrax
people.summary: Co-leader of the Greuthungi with Alatheus, perhaps of Alan origin, whose cavalry struck the Roman flank at Adrianople.

people.name: Mallobaudes

roles.t: Comes domesticorum; king of the Franks

people.summary: Frankish king serving as Gratian's comes domesticorum, co-commander in the victory over the Lentienses at Argentaria (378).

people.name: Priarius
people.summary: King of the Lentienses, killed in their defeat at Argentaria.

people.name: Marcellinus
people.summary: Brother of Magnus Maximus who commanded his army at Poetovio in 388.

people.name: Timasius
people.summary: Senior general of Theodosius who commanded the Roman (non-Gothic) troops at the Frigidus; later exiled by Eutropius in 396.

people.name: Bacurius
people.summary: Iberian (Georgian) prince in Roman service who fought at Adrianople and commanded at the Frigidus, where he was killed; Rufinus knew him personally.
